_doc: 20 GuacWizard scenarios — shared between web Node runner and mobile Dart test. Each scenario lists the summary + accounts that `computeWizardScore` receives. Both engines must produce the same score and the same reason set for every scenario. The web /api/guacwizard endpoint also runs the same function so the API and direct-lib paths cannot drift.

scenarios.title: Brand-new user — no statements, no fees, no txns
scenarios.description: Cold start. No accounts, no data, no anything. Score baselines at 50 ('No bank data uploaded yet').

scenarios.title: Clean user — bank data exists, zero interest + fees, debt down
scenarios.description: Has accounts, paid off card in full, no interest, no fees, refunds + payments cover purchases. Score pegs 100.

scenarios.title: Carrying a small balance — moderate interest
scenarios.description: $50 in interest this period, no fees, no debt growth. -5 interest penalty → score 95.

scenarios.title: Heavy interest — penalty hits the -35 cap
scenarios.description: $600 interest in a single period. (interest/10) = 60, capped at 35. Score drops 35.

scenarios.title: Moderate fees — late + foreign txn
scenarios.description: $50 in fees, no interest, no debt growth. (fees/5) = 10 penalty. Score 90.

scenarios.title: Heavy fees — penalty hits the -20 cap
scenarios.description: $500 in fees (annual fee + multiple foreign txn fees). (fees/5) = 100, capped at 20. Score drops 20.

scenarios.title: Debt grew this period
scenarios.description: $500 purchases, $50 payments, no refunds → netDebtChange = $450. (netDebt/50) = 9 penalty. Score 91.

scenarios.title: Debt growth penalty hits the -20 cap
scenarios.description: $2000 purchases minimal payments → netDebt $1800. (netDebt/50) = 36, capped at 20.

scenarios.title: Debt shrunk — small bonus
scenarios.description: $200 paid down (more payments than purchases). +2 bonus from |netDebt|/100 = 2.

scenarios.title: Big debt paydown — bonus capped at +10
scenarios.description: Paid down $1500. |netDebt|/100 = 15, capped at 10. Bonus alone bumps a 100 → still 100 (max).

scenarios.title: Single card above 25% APR
scenarios.description: One card has 28% APR (predatory). -5 penalty. Score 95.

scenarios.title: Three cards above 25% APR — -15 hit
scenarios.description: Three high-APR cards (cap-2 + retail card + emergency card). 3 × 5 = 15 penalty.

scenarios.title: Compound pain — interest + fees + high APR
scenarios.description: $80 interest, $30 fees, 27% APR card. Penalties: -8 interest, -6 fees, -5 APR = -19 → score 81.

scenarios.title: Interest + fees + growing debt — heavy hit
scenarios.description: $100 interest, $50 fees, $400 net debt growth, 26% APR. -10 interest, -10 fees, -8 debt, -5 APR = -33 → 67.

scenarios.title: Pathological worst case — every penalty fires + clamps at 0
scenarios.description: Massive interest + massive fees + huge debt growth + four 30% APR cards. All penalties cap individually: -35 (interest) -20 (fees) -20 (debt) -20 (4 cards × 5) = -95. Score floor is 0, so a 100→5 result confirms the floor isn't being hit (we're testing it's not crossed). If accounts had been 5+ cards the score would hit 0.

scenarios.title: Best case — clean user + debt down + low APR — score clamps at 100
scenarios.description: Zero interest, zero fees, paid down $800, every card under 20% APR. Bonus alone would push past 100 → clamped to 100.

scenarios.title: Fees imported but no statements — synthetic-account fallback
scenarios.description: User has bank_fees rows but no bank_statements. Old code returned baseline 50; the synthetic-account fallback now scores from the raw fee total. $90 fees → -18 penalty → score 82.

scenarios.title: Only purchases logged — no debt-growth penalty
scenarios.description: $300 purchases, $300 payments (paid in full). netDebt = 0, no penalty.

scenarios.title: Refunds reduce net debt change (no growth penalty)
scenarios.description: $600 purchases, $400 refunds, $100 payments. netDebt = 600 - 400 - 100 = 100 → at boundary, no growth penalty (rule is >100).

scenarios.title: Field-name compat — totalPurch (web) vs totalPurchases (mobile)
scenarios.description: Engine accepts both spellings. Synthetic input here uses totalPurch (web spelling) with no totalPurchases. Score should still compute correctly.
